name: CANADA

flag.title: The Maple Leaf
flag.note: Red, white, red — maple leaf centre

lead: Canada is the second-largest country on Earth. Yet few people live in most of it. It has the longest coastline on Earth. A moose can walk for days in its forests without seeing a road.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Canada covers nearly 10 million km². The Rocky Mountains tower in the west. Flat grassy prairies roll through the middle. The ancient Canadian Shield, made of hard rock, covers almost half the country.
The Great Lakes hold one-fifth of all surface fresh water on Earth. Canada has more lakes than any other country, roughly two to three million.
animals: The moose is the world's largest deer. It loves Canada's boreal forests (cold northern forests). A male stands taller than a horse at the shoulder and can swim across a lake.
Each autumn, polar bears gather near Churchill, Manitoba. They wait for Hudson Bay to freeze. The beaver is the national animal. Its dams make ponds for dozens of other species.
culture: Canada has two national languages, English and French. In Québec province, even cereal boxes must show French.
Ice hockey is almost a religion here. The first organised game was played in Montreal in 1875. Canada makes 75% of the world's maple syrup.
history: The First Nations and Inuit are Canada's first peoples. They have lived here for at least 15,000 years. French and British settlers arrived in the 1500s and 1600s. They brought deadly diseases.
Canada became a self-governing country on 1 July 1867. Four provinces joined into a union. Nunavut, a vast Arctic territory, joined in 1999. That completed today's 10 provinces and 3 territories.
wows: Canada's 202,080 km coastline, the longest on Earth, could circle the globe five times.
Mount Logan in Yukon is North America's second-tallest peak, at 5,959 m.
Canada has the most donut shops per person.
The CN Tower was the world's tallest free-standing structure from 1975 to 2007.
Arctic Nunavut is bigger than Western Europe, but has only about 40,000 people.
Canada and the USA share the longest undefended border, at 8,891 km.
James Naismith, a Canadian, invented basketball in 1891 with a peach basket.

myths.myth: Canada is freezing cold all year
myths.fact: Vancouver has mild, rainy winters. Prairie summers often hit 35 °C.

myths.myth: Canadians end every sentence with eh
myths.fact: People use eh to ask for agreement. Most Canadians say it only sometimes.
